llm.summary: The skill largely matches its stated purpose (using Parallel.ai via python scripts), but there are inconsistencies — notably an extra credential (BROWSERUSE_API_KEY) referenced in the runtime instructions that is not declared, and shipped executable scripts with no install spec — so review before installing.

dimensions.detail: The name/description, required python3 binary, and primaryEnv PARALLEL_API_KEY align with a Parallel.ai client. Examples and APIs shown (Search, Task, FindAll, Extract, Monitor) are coherent with a web-research integration.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs use of an additional credential (BROWSERUSE_API_KEY) for authenticated/private sources and shows commands that send data to webhooks and extract paywalled/private content. BROWSERUSE_API_KEY is referenced in examples but is not declared in requires.env, and the skill can accept webhook endpoints which could transmit extracted data externally — these are functionality-relevant but expand the scope beyond the declared env requirements and deserve explicit disclosure.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (instruction-only) but multiple Python script files are present in the bundle and intended to be executed. That isn't inherently malicious, but it's inconsistent: the package includes executable code but doesn't declare how it's installed or sandboxed. You should review those scripts before running them.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The declared primary credential PARALLEL_API_KEY is appropriate. However, SKILL.md references BROWSERUSE_API_KEY for authenticated/private sources (not listed in required env) and shows workflows that may use session-stored credentials via an MCP service. This missing declared env and the potential to access private/internal sources is disproportionate without explicit declaration and justification.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Privilege posture is reasonable: always is not set, the skill is user-invocable, and disable-model-invocation is true (the model cannot call it autonomously). No config paths requested and no persistent system-level privileges are declared.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to implement a Parallel.ai client and needs your PARALLEL_API_KEY — that part is coherent. Before installing: 1) Ask/verify the publisher/source (there's no homepage) and confirm why BROWSERUSE_API_KEY is needed and whether it will be required at runtime. 2) Inspect the included scripts (scripts/*.py, scripts/parallel.sh) for network destinations, credential handling, and any file I/O — they will run with whatever permissions the agent grants. 3) Be cautious about providing BROWSERUSE_API_KEY or other session credentials and about using webhook URLs (they will receive extracted content). 4) If you need private-source support, request that the skill explicitly declare all required env vars and document how private credentials/sessions are stored and transmitted. If you cannot review the scripts or verify the publisher, treat this as higher risk and avoid installing or running it with sensitive credentials.
